intro.title: About Sarzhyn Yar
intro.seoLead: Welcome to **Sarzhyn Yar (Саржин Яр)**, the leafy public park that serves as the green heart of **Kharkiv**, **Kharkiv Oblast**, **Ukraine**. This destination is a primary hub for locals and travelers visiting the region.
intro.description: Sarzhyn Yar is located in Kharkiv, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine. It is a beautiful urban park that serves as an ideal place for locals and tourists to relax and unwind. With its rich greenery and pleasant environment, the park is one of the important green spaces in Kharkiv, providing not only leisure space for citizens but also an excellent vantage point to experience the natural charm of Kharkiv.

history.title: History & Significance of Sarzhyn Yar
history.lead: More than a park, Sarzhyn Yar is a piece of Kharkiv's natural heritage shaped by centuries of spring water flowing toward the city.
paragraphs: Sarzhyn Yar is a historic ravine (yar) more than 12 kilometers long on the northern edge of Kharkiv. Its slopes have carried crystal-clear spring water toward the city for centuries, and the green valley has long been one of Kharkiv's most treasured natural landscapes.

The ravine's most famous feature is the Sarzhyn Yar mineral spring, which still flows today. Around it, a modern spring pavilion and elevated wooden boardwalks have turned the valley into a year-round urban retreat where visitors can drink fresh mineral water, rest in the shade of old trees and enjoy the sound of the stream.

Today Sarzhyn Yar is maintained as a public recreation zone with walking paths, playgrounds, a stream and a small swimming pool. It is a natural monument of local significance and one of the most recognizable green landmarks in Kharkiv.

The dome-shaped concrete spring pavilion that still marks Sarzhyn Yar today was built in the 1960s. The mineral water from this source has been known in Kharkiv for decades under the name «Kharkivska-1» (Харківська-1). The slopes of the ravine border the Kharkiv Botanical Garden, which is why rare plants — including species from the Red Book of Ukraine — have been preserved here.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before visiting Sarzhyn Yar.

items.a: Sarzhyn Yar is located in Kharkiv, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine (postal code 61000), a short walk from Botanichnyi Sad metro station.

items.q: Is Sarzhyn Yar free to visit?
items.a: Yes. Sarzhyn Yar is a public park and is free to visit year-round. No admission ticket or reservation is required.

items.q: What are the opening hours of Sarzhyn Yar?
items.a: Sarzhyn Yar is an open-air park, usually accessible in daylight (roughly 06:00–22:00) and free. Observe the curfew and official restrictions; early mornings are the calmest time for a walk.

items.q: What can visitors do at Sarzhyn Yar?
items.a: Visitors can stroll along the wooden boardwalks, taste natural mineral water at the spring pavilion, use the playground areas, picnic on the lawns or relax beside the stream.

items.q: How do I get to Sarzhyn Yar?
items.a: Take the Kharkiv metro to Botanichnyi Sad station and walk a few minutes to the park. Buses and taxis also stop near the entrances, and the Kharkiv cable car runs across the ravine.

items.q: Is Sarzhyn Yar suitable for families with children?
items.a: Yes. Sarzhyn Yar has playground areas, gentle walking paths and a small swimming pool, making it a family-friendly destination in Kharkiv.

items.q: How do I get to Sarzhyn Yar by metro?
items.a: Take the metro to Botanichnyi Sad station; the park is about a 5-minute walk away. Head towards the green area and the ravine’s wooden boardwalks.

items.q: Which district of Kharkiv is Sarzhyn Yar in?
items.a: Sarzhyn Yar is located in Kharkiv’s Shevchenkivskyi District, in the Pavlovo Pole area to the north-west of the city centre.

items.q: Can I drink the mineral water from the Sarzhyn Yar spring?
items.a: Yes, the water at the spring pavilion is free and intended for drinking. It is best to fill your bottle at the official pavilion rather than from the open stream. If you have chronic health conditions or special needs, consult a doctor before regularly consuming mineral water.

items.q: What should I bring for a walk at Sarzhyn Yar?
items.a: Comfortable shoes (some paths have slopes), drinking water, a hat in summer, an umbrella or light raincoat in spring and autumn, and a camera — the ravine is photogenic all year round.

items.q: How can I check the current status and safety of visiting?
items.a: Sarzhyn Yar is an open public park, but conditions can change. Before you travel, check official announcements from local authorities and guidance on air-raid alerts, as well as the up-to-date tourism information on the official portals listed in the ‘Sources’ section.

seasons.title: Visiting by season: a year-round strategy
seasons.subtitle: How the weather, water, plants and visitor numbers at Sarzhyn Yar change through the year — pick the best time for your trip.
seasons.dataNote: This overview summarises long-term average climate figures for Kharkiv (30-year climate normals) together with the park's seasonal patterns.

items.climate: Cold, averaging −7 to −1 °C, with frequent snowfall and short daylight hours.
items.water: Spring water flows all year round and stays cool; the pavilion works, the pool is closed.
items.nature: Trees are bare and birds winter in the city. The park is quiet and snow-covered.
items.visit: Bring warm clothes and non-slip shoes; paths may be slippery. Mornings are the calmest.

items.climate: Gradual warming from about 0 °C in March to +15–20 °C in May, with rain and snowmelt.
items.water: After the snowmelt the stream and springs run fullest; right after high water the water is more turbid.
items.nature: The first flowers open and grass turns green; birds fill the park — a good time for watching.
items.visit: April–May is a comfortable window: not hot and less crowded. Bring a light waterproof jacket.

items.climate: Warm, averaging +20–25 °C, with possible thunderstorms; July has the most sunny days.
items.water: Water is pleasant to drink at the pavilion; the small pool opens in warm weather (swim at your own risk).
items.nature: Lush greenery, chicks and butterflies; tree shade offers relief from the heat. The most active season for flora.
items.visit: Come early morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat and crowds; carry your own water.

items.climate: Mild cooling from about +18 °C in September to +5 °C in November, with changeable cloud cover.
items.water: Springs remain stable; the water is especially clear in autumn.
items.nature: Golden leaves and crimson maples make the park ideal for photography and quiet walks.
items.visit: September is one of the best months: comfortable temperatures and beautiful scenery.

responsibility.learnTitle: What to know about Sarzhyn Yar

learn.title: A ravine shaped by water
learn.text: The valley is a natural ravine formed by underground and surface water over millennia. The stream in the park is a living part of that process, not a decorative feature.

learn.title: Mineral water from deep below
learn.text: The pavilion water is natural mineral water rising from deep aquifers. It reaches the surface at a stable temperature all year round.

learn.title: A protected natural site
learn.text: Sarzhyn Yar holds the status of a natural monument of local significance, preserving valuable soils, plants and water ecosystems within the city.

duties: Leave the area clean: use the bins or take your rubbish with you.
Do not light open fires outside designated areas.
Do not disturb or feed birds and animals.
Do not pick plants or damage trees; stay on the paths.
Supervise children near the water, stream and pool.
Drink only from the purpose-built pavilion, not from open water bodies.
Respect other visitors: avoid loud music and keep personal space.
responsibility.note: Tip: for the best experience visit on weekday mornings or evenings, when the park is quieter and the light is softer.
